claims.statement: For each eligible ordinary tree and fixed strict favorable-leaf selector, the aggregate S has the exact fixed-selector weighted-layer representation S=sum_{B in I_{p+1}(T)} w_F(B)-sum_{A in I_p(T)} w_F(A). For a concrete (T,p), a saturating cross-tag one-vertex-deletion flow with upper supplies w_F(B) and lower capacities w_F(A) exists if and only if every deletion-neighborhood cut X satisfies sum_X w_F <= sum_{N_-(X)} w_F; such a flow certifies S<=0. The universal cut inequalities are not established here.
claims.scope: The registered lower-region ordinary-tree aggregate with x(T)+2<=p, 3p<2alpha(T)+1, original strict selector F(T,p), original supports and neighborhoods, and repeated leaves counted separately. The flow characterization applies to each such fixed finite instance; no universal sign conclusion is claimed.
claims.reason: The tagwise bijection audits the supplied global weight identity. Integral max-flow/min-cut gives an exact primal and weighted Hall cut dual permitting transfers between supports. The universal cuts remain unproved, and no eligible cut failure or positive aggregate is exhibited.

limitations: No proof that all weighted deletion cuts hold for every eligible tree, and no eligible tree cut failure was computed.
Failure of a proper cut would refute this flow certificate only, not the scalar aggregate; the full-layer cut is the desired scalar inequality itself.
The reduction preserves the original strict selector and repeated leaf tags but does not establish either primary rank guard or favorable-set values for any new instance.
